effectzones: design notes

Source: DESIGN.md

Prototype, version 0.0.0.9000. This file records scope decisions, open questions and unfinished work.

Principle

The package draws a background; it never looks at the estimates. Where a choice has interpretive consequences the conservative option is implemented and documented.

Scope decisions

Deliberately out of scope

  • No classification of estimates or intervals. There is no function that assigns an estimate or a CI to a zone, labels results as “meaningful” or “likely beneficial”, or computes the probability that an effect lies in a zone. That is magnitude-based inference (Batterham & Hopkins 2006), criticised by Welsh & Knight (2015) and Sainani (2018). The vignette explains this to users.
  • No combined ES + MCID background in v0.1. Two backgrounds in one panel would be unreadable and invite reading one scale through the other. Use facets or two plots.
  • No default benchmark set in geom_es_zones(): calling it without thresholds is an error listing es_benchmarks() options. Cohen called his values a fallback.
  • No automatic MCID. A distribution-based value requires an explicit mcid_distribution() call and is marked provisional in the legend.

Implementation choices

  • Zones are layer parameters, not aesthetics. A stat computes the zone rectangles per panel in the scale’s transformed space and returns them in columns ggplot2 does not treat as positions, so the scales are not trained (expand = FALSE). With expand = TRUE the same rectangles are returned as xmin/xmax (or ymin/ymax), so every finite boundary trains the scale. The geom clips to the panel range from coord$backtransform_range() and delegates drawing to GeomRect, which handles coord_flip(), facets and coord limits.
  • Lazy layer construction. geom_es_zones()/geom_mcid_zones() return an effectzones_zones object that becomes a layer plus a manual scale in ggplot_add(). This lets plot_contrasts() fill a missing sd from the model before the layer is built.
  • Legend through private aesthetics (es_zone, mcid_zone) with a manual scale, so the zones never interfere with a fill scale used by other layers. Zone colours (including interpolated transition slices) are carried in a non-aesthetic column.
  • Soft boundaries are n_slices rectangles interpolated in CIELAB (scales::colour_ramp()). Transition width is softness times the threshold (on the log scale for ratio zones), centred on the threshold. Neighbouring transitions that would overlap are shrunk to the midpoint.
  • MCID thresholds are positions on the difference scale relative to the null (lower < 0 < upper); direction decides which side is benefit. A length-2 value is an uncertain threshold, drawn as a fade across the range. beyond = "multiples" deepens the colour at 2x and 3x the MCID, capped at 3x. It requires point thresholds: with a range MCID the multiples would be uncertain as well, and sharp lines at 2x/3x would overstate precision, so the combination is an error (decided by the author over fading the multiples, which overlap for wide ranges).
  • MCID default palette: the muted blue/orange diverging palette ("diverging"), confirmed by the author; "grey" remains available with labels = TRUE recommended.
  • Zone labels (labels = TRUE) are dropped at draw time when the text does not fit inside its zone, rather than overlapping.
  • plot_contrasts() and the SD. Standardised thresholds over raw differences need an SD. The model’s residual SD is used automatically only for a one-way, fixed-effects, unweighted linear model, where it is the pooled within-group SD (the conventional denominator of d, under the same equal-variance assumption as the ANOVA and Tukey intervals). With more terms the residual SD has every other term’s variance removed: right for manipulated factors, too small for measured factors and covariates, and the model does not record which is which. The function stops with an error that teaches the procedure: decide what SD the benchmark refers to; prefer an external pre-specified SD; otherwise refit with only the manipulated factors (Olejnik & Algina 2003 generalized standardizer); report the SD’s sampling uncertainty. The model can come from an aov fit, an emmeans grid of means (which carries sigma), or a TukeyHSD object: its stored call is re-evaluated in the calling environment and the refit is accepted only if it reproduces the Tukey contrasts exactly. emmeans contrast grids drop sigma, so they need model = or sd.
  • Chen et al. odds ratios. chen_or_thresholds(baseline_risk) implements p1 = Phi(Phi^-1(p0) + d) and OR = odds(p1) / odds(p0); it reproduces the published 1% and 5% rows. Under this model the protective side is not the reciprocal of the harmful side (except at p0 = 0.5), so the boundaries below 1 are computed from negative d (cuts_lower). The published values cover only OR > 1; the lower side in es_benchmarks("chen_or") (1.74, 4.28, 11.40, rounded) is computed, not published, and the source text says so.
  • Legend shows only visible zones. The stat drops zones that lie entirely outside the axis range trained so far (including the scale’s expansion). Coordinate limits (coord_cartesian(xlim)) and ranges created later by other layers’ stats are not known at that stage, so in those cases the legend can list a zone that is clipped away.
  • Renaming zones: zone_labels on both layers, either a full unnamed vector/list or a named partial mapping.
  • Extra arguments beyond the specification: label_size, label_colour, n_slices, zone_labels, title, show.legend on both layers; cuts_lower on es_thresholds(); chen_or_thresholds(); mcid (symmetric shorthand) on mcid_thresholds(); direction on mcid_distribution(); which, model, null, xlab, conf.level on plot_contrasts() methods, and an aov method.

Open questions

  • Drawing the SD’s sampling uncertainty (step 4 of the SD procedure). The boundaries d x SD could fade across d x [lower, upper] of the SD’s confidence interval (chi-square interval on the residual df), reusing the range-MCID fade. Not implemented; the error message and vignette tell users to report it.

  • A measured = helper, e.g. pooled_sd(model, measured = "sex"), that refits without the named terms. Currently users call pooled_sd(update(model, . ~ treatment)) themselves.

  • Some users may prefer that chen_or_thresholds() also accept the baseline risk of the exposed group (i.e. odds ratios expressed the other way round); currently baseline_risk must refer to the reference (denominator) group.

Unfinished / known limitations

  • Development environment. The prototype was built in a sandbox whose R package mirror was unavailable; the system packages provided ggplot2 3.4.4, below the declared ggplot2 (>= 3.5.0). Local R CMD check --as-cran and tests were run against 3.4.4 with the floor temporarily relaxed in a scratch copy; GitHub Actions checks against current CRAN releases.
  • vdiffr snapshots are per ggplot2 version (_snaps/ggplot2-X.Y/). References exist for ggplot2 3.4 (recorded in the development sandbox) and 4.0 (recorded on GitHub Actions, ubuntu-latest, R 4.6.1, then reviewed). Snapshot tests are skipped when no reference exists for the installed version; to add one, run the tests with EFFECTZONES_RECORD_SNAPSHOTS=true (and CI=false, since recent testthat fails on new snapshots on CI) and review with testthat::snapshot_review().
  • Non-linear coordinate systems (coord_polar(), coord_trans()) are not tested.
  • Seams between transition slices: with semi-transparent fills, some PDF viewers may show hairlines between adjacent slices at extreme zoom.
  • DOIs for all cited references are included. Funder & Ozer (2019), Gignac & Szodorai (2016) and Jaeschke et al. (1989) were verified against bibliographic records during development; the others were supplied by the author.
